newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traders say Thyssen drop an overreaction.
newsitem.headline: Traders say Thyssen drop an overreaction.

text.p: Shares in German steel group Thyssen AG fell about one percent in early dealings after two major construction groups said they would pull out of a controversial high-speed rail project.
Thyssen fell 3.20 marks to 380.20 marks after Hochtief and Holzmann said they were withdrawing from the Transrapid project in northern Germany.
But some traders said the drop in Thyssen was unwarranted and a knee-jerk reaction that failed to reflect the stock's fundamentals and more important position in the steel sector.

"This should not have a major impact on Thyssen," said Michael Broeker at Societe Generale in Frankfurt. "It is more important to focus on their steel industry activities and the prospects for improvement in their operations."
Thyssen recently merged it steel operations with those of rival Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp after Krupp called off its hostile takeover bid for Thyssen.
